summary: A 1960s prefab steel tower in Acadia National Park replaced a 1941 wooden lookout; it is open only when park staff are present, and sources disagree on staffing.

facts.design: Prefabricated steel tower flown in by helicopter in 1960 under Operation Beech, built 1960-62, replacing a CCC-built wooden lookout

staffing.status: Occasional, when park staff are present; NHLR and NPS disagree on whether rangers staff it

access.note: Platform and inside room open to the public when park staff are present, often in summer. Leashed dogs may join hikers on the trails but cannot climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: Hike from the Beech Mountain Parking Lot on park trails. The tower is open only when park staff are present.

facts.agency: National Park Service, Acadia National Park

events.note: Original wooden CCC-built lookout in use from 1941 to the mid-1950s (NPS). NHLR dates the lookout site from 1943.
Wooden lookout was critical to fire warning communications during the Fire of 1947
Steel tower flown in by helicopter as part of Operation Beech, replacing the deteriorating wooden lookout
NHLR lists 1962 as the build year, described as 1960-62. NPS says the lookout was operational again in 1962.
Last time a park ranger manned the tower (NPS). NPS says it has not been manned since.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, September 16, 1993

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the mountain has been the site of a lookout since 1943. NPS says the original wooden tower was in use from 1941. The story gives the NPS date for the wooden tower and the NHLR date for the site.
NHLR gives 1962 in its details and 1960-62 in its description. NPS says the steel tower was flown in in 1960 and was operational again in 1962. The story uses the range.

notes_for_editor: Staffing conflict is unresolved: NHLR says rangers staff it during high fire danger (present tense); NPS says it has not been manned since 1976. The NPS fire towers page was last updated 2020-10-07. Current 2024-2026 opening status was not confirmed by any source I could read. OpenStreetMap node 358231332 tags access=private, which conflicts with NPS; not used. Wikidata gives elevation 833 ft; NHLR gives 807 ft (246 m, matching the brief). Coordinates match NHLR. Registration date September 16, 1993 is confirmed by NHLR and NPS.
